query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models** — The closest direct match: eight multi-turn RL tasks, including conversations with LLM-based user simulators. Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai, and Sergey Levine — UC Berkeley; Kelvin Xu and Sergey Levine — Google DeepMind.  
   URL: [https://lmrl-gym.github.io/](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)

2. **Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning** — Evaluates and trains user simulators for therapy, education, and social dialogue using persona-consistency metrics as multi-turn RL rewards. Marwa Abdulhai and Ryan Cheng — UC Berkeley; Donovan Clay and Tim Althoff — University of Washington; Sergey Levine — UC Berkeley; Natasha Jaques — University of Washington and Google DeepMind.  
   URL: [https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00222)

3. **SWEET-RL / Collaborative Agent Bench (ColBench)** — A benchmark in which agents collaborate over multiple turns with a simulated human on programming and frontend-design tasks; SWEET-RL supplies step-level credit assignment. Yifei Zhou, Song Jiang, Yuandong Tian, Jason Weston, Sergey Levine, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, and Xian Li — UC Berkeley and FAIR/Meta.  
   URL: [https://github.com/facebookresearch/sweet_rl](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sweet_rl)

4. **SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?** — A 909-conversation benchmark measuring whether simulated users reproduce human behavior and human judgments in tutoring and document-creation tasks. Yao Dou, Alan Ritter, and Wei Xu — Georgia Institute of Technology; Michel Galley, Baolin Peng, Chris Kedzie, Weixin Cai, Chris Quirk, and Jianfeng Gao — Microsoft.  
   URL: [https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1786/](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1786/)

5. **τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains** — A widely used multi-turn customer-service environment featuring an LLM-simulated user, tool APIs, policy constraints, and outcome-based evaluation; highly relevant as an RL environment even though the original paper focuses on evaluation. Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, and Karthik Narasimhan — Sierra.  
   URL: [https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12045)

query: editable training systems for tool-using agents
text:
1. **Agent Lightning** — A flexible RL framework that trains existing tool-using agents with almost no code changes; supports LangChain, AutoGen, and OpenAI Agents SDK. People: Xufang Luo, Yuge Zhang, Zhiyuan He, Zilong Wang, Siyun Zhao, Dongsheng Li, Luna K. Qiu, Yuqing Yang — **Microsoft Research**.  
   URL: [arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680)

2. **ToolBrain** — A lightweight, extensible training system supporting editable reward functions, GRPO, DPO, supervised learning, tool retrieval, distillation, and automatic task generation. People: Quy Minh Le, Minh Sao Khue Luu — **ToolBrain Research**; Khanh-Tung Tran, Duc-Hai Nguyen, Hoang-Quoc-Viet Pham, Hoang D. Nguyen — **University College Cork**; Quan Le — **CeADAR/University College Dublin**; Hoang Thanh Lam — **IBM Research Dublin**.  
   URL: [arxiv.org/abs/2510.00023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00023)

3. **ART: Agent Reinforcement Trainer** — An open-source, Python-oriented framework for training multi-step agents using GRPO, with user-defined environments and rewards; includes a tool-using email-research example. People: Brad Hilton, Kyle Corbitt, David Corbitt, Saumya Gandhi, Angky William, Bohdan Kovalevskyi, Andie Jones — **OpenPipe**.  
   URL: [github.com/OpenPipe/ART](https://github.com/OpenPipe/ART)

4. **ARTIST** — A Microsoft Research framework coupling reinforcement learning with dynamic tool invocation; models learn when, how, and which tools to call using outcome-level rewards. People: Joykirat Singh, Raghav Magazine, Yash Pandya, Akshay Nambi — **Microsoft Research**.  
   URL: [arxiv.org/abs/2505.01441](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01441)

5. **GOAT** — A training framework that automatically synthesizes goal-oriented, multi-API tool-use data from API documentation, enabling agent fine-tuning without human annotations. People: Hyunji Min, Junyoung Sung, Dosung Lee, Leekyeung Han, Paul Hongsuck Seo — **Korea University**; Sangwon Jung — **Trillion Labs**.  
   URL: [aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1150](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1150/)
